summary: The seam 4 fix clears SPEC-1 and its three declared failure paths are tested and passing, but the new walker still silently drops dangling symlinks, the root-only skip hides the unreadable-directory test on root runs, and non-cyclic symlink fan-out is unbounded.

findings.summary: _collect_records drops a dangling symlink without any error, so tree_digest returns a digest of a partial tree instead of "unavailable", contrary to its own docstring.
findings.evidence: Line 267 is `elif entry.is_file():` with no else branch. A dangling symlink has is_dir() and is_file() both False, so it is skipped silently. The tree_digest docstring (lines 243-244) promises "unavailable" when anything under the root cannot be read and never the digest of a partial tree. Probe: a tree containing a.txt plus a dangling symlink produced the same digest as the clean tree (both da0fbea065af...), not "unavailable". This is the silent-swallow pattern ENG-17 forbids, in the function this fix rewrote. No test covers it.
findings.fix: Raise OSError for an entry that is neither a directory nor a regular file (for example `else: raise OSError(f"unreadable entry {entry.path}")`, or check entry.is_symlink() first) so safe paths still yield digests and dangling links yield "unavailable". Add a test for a dangling symlink under the root.

findings.summary: The unreadable-subdirectory test is skipped when the euid is 0 with no exemption in the plan, so the declared failure path is not exercised on root runs.
findings.evidence: Line 451 is `@unittest.skipIf(os.geteuid() == 0, "root reads unreadable directories")`. ENG-5 allows a skip only where the plan states the exemption and its reason, and only for documentation or configuration. plan.md seam 4 declares "unreadable subdirectory under root -> unavailable" as a required failure path with no exemption. ENG-1 requires the relevant failure paths to be tested. The test passes as a non-root user (verified locally), so the impact is limited to root or CI runs that would skip it silently.
findings.fix: Make the test deterministic without relying on permissions under root (for example, patch os.scandir to raise PermissionError for the locked directory), or remove the skip and run the test under a non-root runner. If the skip must stay, declare it in the plan with its reason.

findings.summary: The bound only detects symlink cycles along the ancestor chain, so non-cyclic symlink fan-out is re-walked on every path with no overall bound.
findings.evidence: Lines 262-266 pass `(*ancestors, real)` to the recursion and keep no visited set across branches. A directory reachable through many symlink paths that do not form a cycle is walked once per path. The seam text requires a bounded walk (no hang), and ENG-24 asks for bounds on work. This is reasoned from the code and not measured. The impact is limited to an operator-controlled installed or checkout tree.
findings.fix: Keep a visited set of realpaths across the whole walk (or use followlinks=False for directories and treat a symlinked directory as unavailable), and optionally cap total entries, recording "unavailable" on overflow.
